workstream: Wave 3C-1a — Official Makati public-facility inventory baseline
scope: Research and source reconciliation only. No Civic Map facilities are added or removed in this step.
inclusionRule: Track physical, public-facing government/service facilities that are meaningful destinations or civic assets. Do not create separate map assets for every department/counter inside one building, generic personnel counts, or private facilities.
sourcePriority: Current City Government of Makati named facility pages/directories
Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023 for post-transfer current counts
Makati Facts and Figures 2020 and older city plans for named historical inventories
Other official government sources for boundary/control transfers or current operating verification

currentHeadlineBaseline.source: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023
currentHeadlineBaseline.geography: Current Makati excluding the 10 transferred barangays where noted
currentHeadlineBaseline.note: Headline counts establish current scale but do not by themselves identify every current facility.

namedFacilitySources.source: City Government of Makati — Barangay Health Centers
namedFacilitySources.finding: The directory's 13 District I centers plus five District II centers in Guadalupe Nuevo, Guadalupe Viejo, Pinagkaisahan, Poblacion and Valenzuela produce 18 current-Makati names, matching the 2023 headline count of 18 health centers.
currentMakatiNames: Rural Health Unit (RHU) — Pio del Pilar
namedFacilitySources.caveat: Current operating status/address still requires per-site verification before implementation.

namedFacilitySources.source: Makati Facts and Figures 2020 — Public Health Infrastructures
namedFacilitySources.finding: Broader list includes medical/dental centers, satellites, Ospital ng Makati and facilities later transferred to Taguig. It is provenance and alias evidence, not the current 18-center denominator.
namedFacilitySources.caveat: Reconcile facility type and successor names against the narrower 2023 categories before mapping.

namedFacilitySources.source: City Government of Makati — Fire Stations Hotlines
namedFacilitySources.finding: The current named city webpage contains one central station plus ten satellite/substations, exactly matching the 2023 headline count.

namedFacilitySources.source: City Government of Makati — Reporting a Crime and Asking for Police Assistance
namedFacilitySources.finding: Removing the three precincts situated in transferred barangays yields one headquarters plus seven current-Makati precinct/substation candidates, matching the 2023 headline count.

secondaryTransferEvidence.finding: NAPOLCOM records transfer of administrative/operational control for PCPs in the 10 transferred barangays and later transfer of Makati Police Sub-Stations 8 and 9 to Taguig.

namedFacilitySources.caveat: Current precinct numbering, names and exact sites must be reverified before implementation.

namedFacilitySources.source: Makati Facts and Figures 2020 — City-Owned Enterprises / Public Markets
namedFacilitySources.finding: Only Poblacion Public Market remains within present-day Makati from this city-owned-enterprise list.
namedFacilitySources.caveat: Verify current operating status and site before implementation.

namedFacilitySources.source: Makati Facts and Figures 2020 — Day Care Services
namedFacilitySources.finding: Detailed named day-care and child-minding locations exist, but the list predates the boundary transfer and does not cleanly reconcile to the 2023 count of 22 day-care centers plus one child-minding center without a site-by-site continuity check.

namedFacilitySources.source: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023 — Social Welfare
namedFacilitySources.finding: Current counts are authoritative, but the Basic Facts sheet does not provide names/addresses beyond facility type.

findings: The original four-facility 3C-1 batch was a pilot, not a completeness baseline.
Health centers and fire stations have unusually strong named baselines whose current-Makati counts line up with the 2023 official headline counts.
Police facilities have a workable historical named list, but current numbering/locations need verification after the 2023-2024 jurisdiction transfers.
Day-care/community facilities require a separate continuity reconciliation because the detailed named list predates the transfer and does not trivially equal the 2023 current count.
Makati-LGU facility completeness and supplemental national-government service coverage must remain separate counts.
